schemas/release-metadata.schema.json makes contains_ai required with no default in every element block. Rationale: an omitted disclosure is not read as None downstream -- YouTube treats an empty contains_ai as unknown and substitutes its own signals, Deezer tags by detection regardless of declaration, and Spotify states the absence of an AI credit does not mean AI was not used. No default is safe: None is a false negative on an AI catalog, All forfeits Deezer search placement on releases with real human performance, and unknown is a reset mechanism rather than a declarable state. Partly requires a named human_contribution on that element; All forbids one.

decision: Merge Prosecutor Work Requests are GitHub issues titled [WR], not markdown files on the Actions runner. Audrey Evans rejected the empty verification on PR #18276 (needs to actually be worked on). createWR still writes the local file so a tokenless run leaves something a person can read, and so the original behavior stays visible. fileWorkRequest opens or reuses the issue. The search token is mpkey plus a 20-char sha256 prefix because a key:value line is parsed as a GitHub search qualifier. A 403 is returned and logged; fork pull requests cannot open issues with the default GITHUB_TOKEN. The finding sets the job exit code before the API call, so a failed create cannot turn a bad merge green. The browser page at docs/merge-prosecutor/ runs the same detectors and does not open issues.
